content.label: Feature flag rollout guide
content.takeaway: This guide outlines the step-by-step process for Orbit feature flag rollouts.

nodes.title: Purpose of the Guide
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide § text#0

content.markdown: This guide is intended for engineers responsible for managing feature flags within the Orbit platform. It outlines the process of transitioning a feature flag from an 'off' state to a fully 'on' state, detailing the prerequisites for each step.

nodes.title: Scope
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide § text#1

content.markdown: This guide specifically addresses feature flag rollouts and does not cover experiments, which have a separate process.

nodes.title: Conditions for Progression
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide § text#2

content.markdown: Each subsequent section of this guide will specify the conditions that must be met before a feature flag can advance to the next stage of its rollout.

nodes.title: Support
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide § text#3

content.markdown: For any questions regarding this guide, please contact the platform team.

nodes.title: Takeaway
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide § text#4

content.markdown: This guide outlines the step-by-step process for Orbit feature flag rollouts.

content.label: Rollout stages
content.takeaway: Rollout proceeds through internal, canary, and general availability stages with checks at each step.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § shape#0

Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#0

content.markdown: The flag is active only for staff accounts, allowing internal problem detection before customer exposure. This stage typically lasts one working day, with no minimum duration specified.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § shape#1

Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#1

content.markdown: A small percentage (5%) of real traffic is exposed to the change, selected randomly per request. This stage must last at least 30 minutes to cover a full traffic cycle of the slowest endpoint. Manual percentage changes during this period reset the measurement window, and short canaries are a common cause of problematic flags reaching general availability.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § shape#2

Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#2

content.markdown: This check compares the error rate and p95 latency of flagged requests against the same requests from the previous 7 days. It runs automatically at the end of the canary window. If the check fails, the flag remains in canary for owner investigation.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § shape#3

Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#3

content.markdown: The flag is progressively enabled for all users in steps of 25%, 50%, and 100%. During this ramp-up, the owner monitors the error dashboard, which displays flagged and unflagged requests side-by-side to identify flag-specific issues. The owner continues monitoring until the flag has been at 100% for one hour, paging the on-call engineer if errors increase.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#4

content.markdown: Each stage's progress is recorded in the rollout tool, maintaining a history of who moved the flag and when.

nodes.title: Rollout Flow Summary
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary ⨁ Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability § text#5

content.markdown: The rollout process follows a sequential progression through three distinct stages: Internal, Canary, and General Availability. Advancement between stages is contingent on successful monitoring and automated checks, particularly the metrics check before General Availability. The process emphasizes early problem detection and controlled exposure to minimize customer impact.

nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch § group#0

content.label: Kill switch
content.takeaway: Every flag needs a tested, quickly-acting kill switch for safe rollouts.

nodes.title: Kill Switch Requirement
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch § text#0

content.markdown:
- Every flag must have a kill switch.
- The kill switch must turn off the flag within 1 minute.

nodes.title: Testing and Approval
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch § text#1

content.markdown:
- The kill switch must be tested in staging before the flag enters canary.
- The test must be recorded in the rollout tool.
- A flag without a tested kill switch cannot enter canary.
- Any member of the owning team can use the kill switch without approval.

nodes.title: Kill Switch Safety and Re-enabling
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch § text#2

content.markdown:
- Turning a flag off using the kill switch is always safe.
- Turning a flag back on restarts the rollout from the internal stage.

nodes.title: Importance of Kill Switches
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch § text#3

content.markdown: Kill switches are critical. The policy emphasizes pre-deployment testing and immediate team-wide access to minimize risk during feature rollouts.

nodes.title: Process Overview
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup § text#0

content.markdown: This flow outlines the process for removing feature flags after they have been fully rolled out. It includes a mechanism for tracking flags that miss their cleanup deadline.

nodes.title: Goal
nodes.stableKey: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup § text#1

content.markdown: The primary goal is to maintain code quality by removing obsolete feature flags, which otherwise hinder readability and slow down future development.
